<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines only standard metadata variables and source arrays at the top-level scope (pkgname, pkgver, depends, source, sha256sums, etc.). All actual build/execution logic is contained inside function definitions (_check_electron, prepare, build, package, etc.) which are NOT executed when the PKGBUILD is sourced by `makepkg --printsrcinfo`.

There are no top-level command substitutions, no eval, no curl/wget, and no obfuscated or encoded payloads in the global scope. The source array references the package's own upstream repository (github.com/Foundry376/Mailspring and Foundry376/Mailspring-Sync) and the official Electron artifact server (artifacts.electronjs.org), all of which are expected sources for this package.

One checksum is set to 'SKIP' for the Mailspring-Sync git source, which is standard practice for VCS sources and is not grounds for concern. No sources are downloaded or verified during `makepkg --printsrcinfo`, so the SKIP checksum does not affect this gate.

Since sourcing the PKGBUILD only assigns variables and defines functions without executing any potentially dangerous code, running `makepkg --printsrcinfo` is safe.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>
Top-level scope only defines variables and functions; no malicious code runs during sourcing.
</summary>
</security_assessment>

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>

The script then executes the Electron runtime with the application bundle (`app.asar`). There is no code that downloads or executes external content, no obfuscation, no suspicious network requests, and no operations outside the application's expected scope. The variable substitutions (`@PKGNAME@`, `@ELECTRON@`) will be replaced at package build time, and the script itself contains no supply-chain risk.
